  x1.3). Style "slingshot" (two-handed: the fork in the right hand, the pouch in the left), at the hip put away.
- **The stance** (GunMoves "sl_*", keyed arms, no grip channels): side on with the right shoulder leading, the fork low
  ahead, the pouch pinched behind it; drawn, the fork arm straight out at the target and the pouch at the left cheek.
  **The band** (GunMoves.sling_band, each frame on a slingshot body after posing): two stretched strands from the prong
  tips to the left hand while it's out (one shared box mesh, two transforms a frame), hidden put away.
- **The stone** (scripts/weapons/sling_arts.gd through ShootState): left click draws and looses (sl_shot, 0.36 s x
  speed; the stone leaves at 0.2 s): Shell "pellet" at 46 m/s on the low arc to the reticle, 9 damage, a 0.25 s
  stagger, no reload ever (the HUD shows no loads). Right click held is the power draw (HeavyAttackState
  "power_draw", cfg "arts": SlingArts.heavy_enter / heavy_update): two levels at 0.4 / 0.9 s (Quick Draw sooner), let
  go (or 1.6 s) a "pellet_big": 14 / 24 / 36, the full draw knocks down. Skid Shot at a sprint (a slide, three stones
  fanned); Hail Shot in the air (three fanned down at the reticle); parry/block with the hands up crossed.
- **Trick ammo** (a round's `extra`: "fire" / "smoke" / "blast" / "sticky", "@k" its strength x the design's "trick" and
  trick_ stats; SlingArts.burst where it lands): fire (a 2.2 m burst, 10, burning 4 s), smoke (a 4 m cloud: everyone in
  it staggered 2 s "Blinded", you slip out of sight if you're in it), blast (2.6 m, 20, knockdown), sticky (3 m: rooted
  3 s via `root_enemy`, "Stuck!"). Each is a technique (Fire / Smoke / Blast / Sticky Pellet); Bag of Tricks (ult,
  untouchable) fires five at the foes ahead, a trick each at x1.6. Trick Pouch: every fifth stone a random trick at half.
- **Tree** (SkillTrees "slingshot": Tricks / Aim / Pouch, element "sl" the trickster's spark): Fire Pellet 4 · Smoke
  Pellet 8 · Trick Pouch 14 · Nasty Surprises 20 (trick_ +30%); Blast Pellet 5 · Sticky Pellet 10 · Bag of Tricks 30;
  Skid Shot 2 · Quick Draw 4 (draw_) · Hail Shot 6 · Sharpshooter 13 (passive) · Trickster's Way 22 (Prankster / Sure
  Shot). Steps 30. New keys: trick_, draw_, pouch_.
- **FX**: TREE_FX "slingshot" (pale pink core, hot-pink edge, tangerine accent); element / elem_hit pink sparks and
  tangerine motes. Pellets wear their trick's colour (a fire pellet glows). Sounds: whoosh + slap on the loose, rope
  creaking on the draw, the tricks' own (fire_burst, thud, cannon_hit, splash).
- **Sources**: IslandContent.LOOT_WEAPONS and IslandEncounters.LOOT "slingshot"; never turned into a greatsword by a
  chest; Shops.RARE_KINDS; Haldor's pool slingshot / vine / bone / iron@1; the Shift+F10 rack. Trait: hair-trigger.
- **Co-op**: stones are Shells (harmless copies on the other screens), hits through Hurtbox.take_hit, `rooted` through
  its HOST_CALLS forward, effects through Net.fx. **Per frame**: the band on slingshot bodies (two transforms); a stone
  in flight a shape query and a ray a tick.

## 2026-10-28: the banjo, a sixth instrument (v1.25)

- **Why a banjo:** the five were a reed (concertina), a bow (fiddle), a flute (whistle), a drum (bodhran) and a
  wheel drone (gurdy); nothing was picked. The banjo is the bright, quick-fading plucked voice the band lacked and a
  sailors' instrument. (A cornet was built alongside and dropped when 1.25 was trimmed to one instrument.)
- **Item:** `Instruments.ITEMS["banjo"]` (id `banjo`, 120 at Corin's, worth 48), in KINDS, so chain traders roll
  it too. Corin's stock (`shops.gd`) and his bark name it.
- **Model** (`Instruments._banjo`, ~5 surfaces): pot centred at the origin, head +Y, neck -Z; resonator, metal rim
  and 16 hooks, the head recessed in a rim ring, neck and fingerboard with 12 frets on the real scale, nut, a
  tilted peghead and four pegs, the short fifth string's peg halfway up, bridge, tailpiece, five strings.
  `BANJO_PICK` / `BANJO_STOP` are where the hands go. Icon from the mesh (fiddle's view).
- **Played** (Jam `"banjo"`, InstrumentPoses `music_banjo`, ActionSpecs): slung across the belly, neck up to the
  left, head out; the right hand bounces a stroke a sub-beat over the head, the left shifts along the neck every
  two. Carried on the back, neck up over the left shoulder.
- **Stems** (`gen_psx_music.py`): `inst_banjo` (bright KS picked near the bridge, the head's honk as a 0.7-1.5 kHz
  band mixed in, a nail click). `_jam_banjo`: the tune picked, each long note rolled a tick at a time (a chord tone
  under it, then the high fifth-string drone, the drone root two octaves up). Sequenced after every other voice so
  the song's rng gives the old stems the same notes (they weren't rewritten). Levelled at -21 LU (`JAM_LU`; the
  picks' attacks carry, loudest 400 ms ~-15 to -18 vs the others' ~-17.5), seams <= 0.003.
  `gen_psx_music.py jam banjo` renders one instrument's stems for every tune.
- jamshot closes the first-launch character creator (it opens in a window when user:// has no look and hung the
  render). Tests: t/jam/stems (new: every kind a whole instrument, every tune a stem per kind, one length),
  t/items/instruments (counts from KINDS now). Renders: tools/dev/out/jam/js_banjo_*.png.

## 2026-10-28: in-game updates and the installer

- **Patcher** (`scripts/game/patcher.gd`, the FIRST autoload): at start-up, before any other game script loads, it
  promotes a waiting download (`user://update/next.pck` + `next.json`, checksum checked) to `patch.pck` and loads it
  with `ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack(..., true)` when its base is the version the build was exported as; then
  sets `application/config/version` to the patch's. Exported games only. It can never be patched itself: keep it tiny
  and free of game classes.
- **Updater** (`scripts/game/updater.gd`, the title screen's): GitHub's latest stable release -> its `update.json`;
  a patch for this base is a menu button "Update to vX (N MB)" (download, checksum, "restart to play it"); otherwise
  "vX is out: get it" opens the release page (the installer).
- **The preset** no longer embeds the pack (`Driftwake.pck` beside the exe) and delta-encodes patches.
- **CI** (`build-windows.yml`): every build makes `Driftwake-Setup.exe` (Inno Setup, `tools/release/driftwake.iss`,
  per-user install, no admin); a stable tag runs `tools/release/make_update.ps1`: a cumulative patch against the base
  the last release names, or a new base (full) when the native library, project settings or Godot changed, the patch
  is over 40% of the base, there's no earlier `update.json`, or `tools/release/NEW_BASE` exists.
- **Test:** `tools/release/update_test.ps1` exports a base, changes a script and an autoload, exports a patch, installs
  it as a waiting download and checks the base build promotes, loads and runs it (first run: 28 KB patch on a 46 MB
  pack). Project-setting changes (autoloads, input, shader globals) can't ride a patch: those make a new base.
- The first release with this is a new base (full download once); 1.25 and earlier have no Patcher.

## 1.26.1, piece 1: sea pacing and the Admiralty chase (2026-10-29, docs/v1_26_plan.md)
- **Why:** Zach's 2-hour co-op playtest. Patrols every 95 s (each Admiralty ship sunk was 5,000 bounty: heat
  snowballed to Dreaded), cutters that never caught an upgraded ship and turned broadside mid-chase (bleeding speed),
  "Escaped" while the crew was boarding them, and almost no pirates (zones up to 320 m off the route, the Admiralty's
  pursuers filling MAX_ATTACKERS, an officer taking every other island from the rival crew).
- **Bounty/heat:** `Bounty.TABLE.admiralty_ship` 5000 -> 1000. `Admiralty.PATROL_EVERY` [0, 0, 420, 300, 240] (none
  while only Wanted). `Admiralty.QUIET` 300 s with no patrol after any hunt ends (`_quiet_until`, set in `_hunt_note`);
  the end banner says "Escaped" only with a ship still afloat that lost her, else "The patrol is beaten".
- **The chase (EnemyShip):** a pursuer's `_max_speed` is max(her own, the crew's live `speed` + CHASE_EDGE 1.0) for
  CHASE_SECS 90 of a chase (`_chase_t`, reset on PATROL/BLOCK; reads the synced `speed`, so it works whoever steers).
  Kinds with `"chaser"` (marine, frigate) carry a bow gun (`_chaser`, a ShipCannon on the centreline so `_side_guns`
  never counts it) fired dead ahead from HUNT (`_try_chaser`: 0.6 s of sparks, then `_chaser_update` fires; chain shot
  per `_wants_chain`, which now compares with her own canvas, not the chase's borrowed speed). A chaser stays in HUNT
  (`_keeps_chasing`) until within BROADSIDE_IN 34 m or the crew is under CHASE_SLOW 6 m/s, and goes back to HUNT from
  BROADSIDE when the crew runs again.
- **The hunt holds:** `EnemyShip._crew_ship` counts a captain within CREW_NEAR 70 m of the crew's ship (swimming,
  boarding), and `pursuing()` includes DECK (captains fighting on her deck).
- **Pirates:** `_attackers()` skips pursuers (MAX_ATTACKERS is pirates only). Sea legs: two zones with chance
  0.55 + lvl*0.02 (was 0.3), placed within 180 m of the route (was 320; changes every leg's layout from its seed).
  `RivalWatch.decide`: the rival crew rolls first; an officer only takes an island no crew came to.
- **Tests:** new `t/ship/marine_chaser`, `t/ship/hunt_holds`; `t/ship/admiralty_hunt` (Wanted has no patrols; the
  quiet after an escape), `t/ship/admiralty_patrol` (1,000), `t/combat/rival_placement` (crew before officer).
  Expect `legtest`/`seatest` to see different leg layouts at prepush.

## 1.26.1, piece 4: poise and knockback (2026-10-29)
- `Poise.CLASSES`: grunt 50 (was 30), elite 80 (was 55), new "player" 60.
- Grunts (`_poise_broken`): a break ragdolls only from RAGDOLL_FROM = Poise.TECH_MIN (techniques, ultimates; plus
  crumples and launches); lighter breaks (kicks, heavies, finishers) are the 1.3 s hard stagger with a 2 m/s shove
  (was 3.5). Knockdown throw clamp(kb*0.45, 2.5, 4.5) + 2.6 up (was 4-8 + 3.2); hitstun shove min(kb*0.4, 2.5) (was 5).
- Captains (`Player._on_hit_received`): human captains get `_own_poise` (Poise "player", made on the first knockdown
  blow): knockdown blows (or poise >= TECH_MIN) drain it, a 0.35 s stagger short of a break, floored on the break,
  then Poise.IMMUNE 4 s when nothing floors you. A grunt's red-glow blow carries poise 999 (always breaks, unless
  immune). Throw clamp(kb*0.45, 2.5, 4.5) + 2.6 up (was max(kb, 3) + 3.5); flinch shove min(kb*0.4, 2.5).
- AI captains (rivals, officers): a launcher that breaks their poise throws them up (Juggle.CARRY + launch), so
  black-leg's knock-up works on them. (Full air juggling of AI captains is not done: they ragdoll up, not the grunt
  AIR state.)
- Enemies by a downed captain: `_lost` already keeps grunts on a Downed target; the smaller throw keeps the ragdoll
  near where they circle.
- Tests: new `t/combat/player_poise`; `t/combat/poise_knockdown` rewritten for 50 poise and the ragdoll threshold.

## 1.25.4 the Brinehollow opening (2026-10-29)
- **What:** the story (`scripts/game/story.gd` STEPS) is 21 steps across the island: find_town, see_gus, see_nessa (she

  (Vey sends you up the long stair), shrine (Master Isao's Edy reading), tomo (his spar on the terrace), ruins (the
  standing stone), grell, see_odile, see_tackett (timber and chitin), forest (split three ironwood deadfall), queen,
  tackett_ship, see_gus_redtide, morrow. Zach's step list wasn't previewed: **assumed** (the plan doc's "Brinehollow
  opening" row still says "Preview first"; the lead marks it, the doc being open in the main checkout).

  resumes on it and skips the new steps before it; an unknown id finishes the story. `trial` (the rack) is saved too.

  of its place, again after twice as far or REARM_SECS after a loss (`bout_done`, from `ArenaBout.result` on the
  captain's machine). ArenaBout kind `"brawl"` (BRAWLER: bare hands, fights at once, spawned on the spot); master

  Tomo) puts a rival more than LEASH_R off the ground and APART_STUCK from the captain back on it after 1.5 s (not
  while ragdolled); a captain more than FORFEIT_R off loses. The tomo step finishes itself if black leg is known.
- **Vey's rack** (`scripts/game/story_rack.gd`, StoryRack, at StarterIsland.RACK by the yard's north fence): eleven
  kinds racked (cutlass, katana, dirk, boarding axe, spear, warhammer, greatsword, pistol, musket, hand cannon,
  slingshot); its talk (Dialogue.define "story_rack", grouped Blades / Two-handed / Guns) takes one down (bag + hands,
  the last one put back) and keeps it (finishes vey_rack). Drills tick a gun's Shoot as the cut.

  into TownMeshes): Master Isao's reading hall (`scripts/props/shrine_terrace.gd`, ShrineTerrace.reading_hall: walk-in,

- **The forest** (`scripts/game/story_deadfall.gd`, StoryDeadfall, `_build_deadfall` after the life pass, seed
  `deadfall`): three fallen trunks 2.6 m off the forest's paths (12-50 m from FOREST, 26+ from the cave, 16 apart); on

  to the nearest unsplit one. The ruins step is the driftstone's talk (`story` hook in driftstone.json).

## 1.25.3, piece 1: the Edy tree (2026-10-29)
- `scripts/progression/edy_tree.gd` (EdyTree): the round tree as data. The core (your Edy type), eight BRANCHES (Iron
  Will, Sense, Captain's Will, Tide, Tempo, Fury, Bond, Infusion) of seven nodes each in SLOTS (ring 1 off the core, two
  paths at rings 2-3 that meet at ring 4, a capstone at 5), and eight BRIDGES between neighbours (a stat between rings 2-3,
  a passive between 3-4, linked to both sides). Kinds: stat and auto -> SkillTrees "auto", equip -> "passive" (slotted),
  ability -> "tech" with its skill. `tiers`: ranks by use ([name, uses, desc, effects], each replacing the last's);
  `switch`: Progression.edy_off turns it off. `why` (read, linked, price), `rank`, `effects`, `use(p, id, n)` (a toast at a
  rank), `of_skill`, `learn_path` (tests and tools: buys the shortest chain to a node).
- `SkillTrees._build_will` builds the Captain tree's Will branch from it (pool "will", pos round the core); the old Will
  paths' nodes are gone, so an old save's Will purchases drop and their Edy comes back to spend (will_earned untouched).
  Progression: `edy_uses`, `edy_off` (saved), `stat()` takes `EdyTree.effects` for Edy nodes, `buy_why` -> EdyTree.why.
- New mechanics: Foresight by itself (`foresight_auto` s; Player._on_hit_received, its dodge counts toward its rank;
  `foresight_slow` a beat of hitstop), Iron Reflex from its node (`iron_reflex`), casts counting toward their node's rank
  (PowerComponent.try_cast -> EdyTree.use), Emission's uses. Infusion: `PowerComponent.edy_infuse(cost)` (Edy Techniques
  +2 energy a technique and the "edy_tech" buff for its blows, Edy Strikes 0.5 a plain blow; Brimming free above 80%);
  `Player.melee_hit` multiplies an infused blow by 1.08 / 1.05 + edy_dense and gives back edy_regain energy (per swing,
  not per landed hit), with a spark in your Edy's colour at the hand (or shin).
- Reinforce sits in Iron Will (slot 2). Roar, Glimpse and the rest keep their skills; the foresight *skill* isn't in the tree
  (Foresight is the passive now).
- Captain page (`SkillMapScreen._draw_edy_tree`): an oval constellation (the panel's width stretches it), branch names out
  past the capstones (side ones anchored outward; Captain's Will as CAPTAIN'S), links lit between owned nodes, shapes by
  kind, a gold rim on what you can buy, dashed when switched off, rank pips. Enter (`_act_edy`): buy / switch / slot. The
  card (`_edy_card_body`): branch and kind, ranks with uses, what Enter does. A/D no longer flips paths.
- Tests: new `t/progression/edy_tree`; t/will/* buy through learn_path; `t/will/reinforce` (an old save's Will
  purchases drop), `t/progression/edy_types`, `t/ui/skills_captain_forks` rewritten for the tree; `t/progression/will_paths`
  and `t/will/open_paths` (the old path rules) removed. skillmapshot films the tree (_will, _will2, _will_sense).

## 1.25.5, piece 1: side work weakens the villain (2026-10-29)
- `IslandArcs` leads: every quest of the island's done (IslandLife `given` + the board's `notices`), every beast miniboss
  down (flag `mini_<kind>`, the host watching its body), the weak spot heard and each townsman freed (`freed<k>`, piece 6)
  is a lead. The host (`_lead_watch`, every TICK, before the arc is even taken) sets `lead<k>` flags for new ones and
  everyone toasts it. A lead's kind is its place in `LEADS` (intel, lieutenant, wound, ally, lieutenant, wound, ally,
  then wounds; a lieutenant on a villain with no crew is a wound). All read from world flags, so a guest and a late
  joiner see the same.
- Effects at the showdown (every machine, `_process` at step n): `_send_off` frees the crew's last plain men (by spec
  index, the same ones everywhere, like the Iron Boot turncoats); `_ensure_allies` puts villagers (`Ally<k>`) by the
  place, who follow the fight (`_follow_fight`) and land one ALLY_BLOW (6%) each (host, `ablow<k>`); wounds add
  LEAD_WOUND (10%) each to the replies' `wounded:` (WOUND_MAX 60%) when he wakes; intel marks the map (MapFog) at once.
- The showdown is open any time: the elder's "Where's X? We'll face him now." jumps the Journal to it, and a camp or
  beast villain brought down early jumps it too. The elder's "About X..." ends with the leads so far (a Dialogue token
  `<key>_leads`); the Journal's showdown goal shows "(N leads)".
- Gossip: the first named villager (not a trader) tells the villain's weak spot (GOSSIP by kind; a lead, into the
  journal's rumours); the second where the beast miniboss dens (its site charted for the crew).
- Reward: the arc's turn-in is gold 120 + 60/tier and `"xp": 4.0` (QuestRewards: XP_SHARE x 4 of a level to every
  captain, wherever they are); the arc chest gets 15 + 5/tier gold a lead and a tonic. Bounty and the Admiralty's answer
  as before. Numbers assumed (docs/v1_26_plan.md).
- Test: `t/quests/arc_leads` (a built jungle island, the Tyrant's Tax).

## 1.25.3, piece 2: the Edy looks (2026-10-29)
- Zach: the whole-body glow and the tall flame were too big and distracting (Storm's worst); he picked the Edy tree mock's
  subtle sketches, plus "a little bit of aura" on the limbs and the whole body for Reinforce.
- `EdyAura` rewritten: no flame card, no hand/foot flame cards. A light outline (the rim shader at RIM_K 0.45, RIM_GROW
  0.015) on the arms (Infuse, big flares) or the whole body (Reinforce); none on the legs (one skin with the body).
  GPUParticles3D per limb, born on a cylinder round it (EMISSION_SHAPE_RING along the bone: forearm down to the hand,

  unique place (kind "unique", `trade` = its id). IslandVillage builds them as `KitHouses.room` with the trade as the
  room's kind (a theme with its own trade model uses that); `KitShops.inside` dresses smith (forge, anvil, quench tub,
  blades), armourer (shields, two armour stands), tailor (bolts, dress form, a rail of garments), luthier (lutes, drums),
  apothecary (bottles, herbs, mortar, scales) behind a counter (Vendor/Customer markers). The trader's routine is their
  shop's Vendor spot (`vshop_<trade>`, IslandLife._routine), any hamlet, all day and night. The store and cookhouse
  were already dressed rooms.

  onsen (20 gold: full heal and the "hot_spring" buff, 30 min), restaurant (a shop of feasts), swordsmith (a shop of
  tier+2 blades with traits), sea shrine (10 gold: "sea_blessing", 20 min), cartographer (40 gold: the whole island
  charted; a treasure chart once), dojo (50 gold: 2 quests' XP once), curio shop (oddities). The two buffs are Food.MEALS

  the keeper (`IslandVillage._unique_keeper`, a step after the building) inside; what an action gives shows through a

- **Tavern games** (`TavernGames`, the node "Tavern" under the village; games and stakes **assumed**): the dicer and the
  wrestler by the inn's door. Dice: best of three 2d6 throws for 10/25/50 (tokens show the throws). Arm wrestling: an
  overlay (`TavernGames.Wrestle`, PixelCanvas, the Talk state): Attack while the sweeping marker's in the band pushes,
  they push back by tier, 14 s, 25 gold. Three wins running: the host gives the crew 10% at the store and the cookhouse

  have a spot) and `_ruins` plans a held village (worker: roof decks over the 3 ruins nearest the old square, crates

## 1.26 weapons: more from every weapon, all 17 kinds (2026-10-29)

Sheet: docs/weapons_126.md (**assumed**, not previewed). Every weapon tree gets, from `WeaponPlus.TREES`
(scripts/progression/weapon_plus.gd, built by `SkillTrees._plus` after the trees):
- **Two ultimates**: the middle branch splits after `<p>_elem2`: today's ultimate (moved up-left, behind a lead-up
  "mech" node with `ult_charge_pct`, *not* gated, so old saves and t/progression/gate_and_buy are as they were) and the
  new one up-right, gated by node `"needs"` (Progression.buy_why: owns any of them) on its lead-up, itself on elem2.
  R holds one; `PowerComponent.equip_why` refuses swapping one ultimate for another while `Player.in_fight()`.
- **Second crew technique**: variant `<p>_crew` (Guard branch, 12) whose second version sets `crew2_<tree>`;
  `CrewTechniques.id()` then returns `WeaponPlus.crew_of(tree)`. Its entry is in `WeaponPlus.CREW` (`CrewTechniques.def`
  reads ALL then CREW). Kinds in `CrewTechniqueState.DUETS`: **setup** (lead pins, cues "finish", the partner blinks
  beside the foe for the finisher), **combined** (lead cues "duet", both strike from opposite sides, the lead's burst on
  everyone round it), **support** (`CrewTechniques.SUPPORT`: energy, reload, the "crew_rally" buff +20% in
  Player.damage_multiplier, a "shielded" mark turning blows in `blow()`, vanish + "slipped"). "stay" duets (long gun,
  cannon) fire from where they stand. A cue that beats the partner's state is kept in `crew_tech.cue`.
- **Alternates**: variants `<p>_alt_air/sprint/heavy` with `"free"` (Progression._free: they come at 8/14/20) and
  `"anywhere"` (set_version off a rest spot); the second version sets `alt_<slot>_<tree>`. `PlayerState.alt_move(slot)`
  picks the move; combat_input / air_attack_input put it in `PlayerState.pending_tech` and enter Technique with no id.
- **Air buttons split** (Zach's addition): air left-click is the aerial (or its alternate), air right-click the plain
  plunge (`PlayerState.plain_plunge`) until node `<p>_airheavy` (move, mastery 10, `airheavy_<tree>`), then the
  aerial heavy (`PlayerState.air_heavy()`); dual pistols keep Gun Rain on either.
- **Bridges**: four "mech" nodes per tree (stat inside 3 pts at 6, the bigger one further out 4 pts at 15), `"bridge"`,
  `"needs"` = the two nodes they sit between (either side). Always-on (not slotted passives) so master_all's slots stay.
- **The moves**: `PlusMoves.MOVES` (data: name, desc, slot, kind, timeline) played by `PlusArts` (first in
  TechniqueState._arts; the op list is its header). Hits go through Player.melee_hit with the move's kind ("" sprint and
  air, "heavy", "skill" for ultimates) so Edy infusion and the tree's bonuses hold; `PlusArts.shape` sets the flags
  (launch / launch2 for juggles, spike, pin, unblock...). Effects through Net.fx (reached via the tree: static funcs),
  poses mirror as any action. Every weapon has a launcher (an alternate). Second ultimates reuse the first's icon
  (Skills "icon") until they have their own.
- Per frame/tick: nothing new outside a move in progress (the Technique state's own update while it plays).
- Tests: t/weapons plus_tree, plus_<weapon> x17 (on t/_plus_moves.gd), plus_launch, plus_air_buttons; t/crew/plus_duets.
  The per-tree tests now expect two ultimates. Expected to need a look at the release check: techtest, airtest
  (right-click in the air is now the plunge), progtest, stamtest, balancetest, nettest (crew duets over the wire).
  Renders: `abilityshot plus:<move> <style>`, the second ultimates by skill id, `crew:<id>`.

## 1.25.x: saves without a limit (2026-10-29)
- `SaveGame`: any number of saves (`slots()` scans for save_N.dat, newest first; `first_free_slot()` is one past the
  highest, so a new game never overwrites). Each save's meta adds game_version, format, `place_of` (an island's name
  ashore, "At sea, near X" off it) and `crew_of` (every other captain who's sailed in it, accumulated). A thumbnail
  save_N.png (256x144, the viewport when saved; not headless) beside it; `delete_slot` removes both. `slot_info` adds
  those plus `compatible` (format not newer, build not newer than this one: Updater.newer).
- `SaveSlotList`: a scrolling list of rows (picture, name/level, fruit/played/saved, place, crew, version with ✓ / ⚠;
  a newer build's save is greyed out), "+ New captain" on top (allow_new; off in the pause menu's Load). Title: New Game
  starts the next free save directly; Host / Join open the list (its new row runs the creator on arrival, so a guest
  needs no save first).
- Test: savetest (the list, the next number, the build, the place).

## 2026-10-29: save backups and small settings (1.26)

## Stale suites after 1.26.1's poise (2026-10-30)
Prepush was red on 12 suites, all from the unpushed 1.26.1 and 1.24.1 changes (stale tests):
- **Knockdown checks:**
  - A grunt (poise 50) goes down/ragdolls only on a technique-weight break (poise >= TECH_MIN); lighter breaks give a
    1.3 s hard stagger.
  - A captain is floored only on a poise break.
  - ragtest, grunttest and guntest now land technique-weight (or 999) blows where they mean a knockdown.
  - wieldtest and axetest accept "flat, or its poise broken" (a break refills poise and sets `immune()`, so a full
    bar can mean broken).
  - guntest's shove and foresttest's charge accept Stagger or Downed on the captain.
  - katanatest wears its grunt to the old 30 poise so a charged draw still crumples it.
  - grunttest heals the grunt before the hit from behind (9 light hits to break 50 poise left it on 2 HP).
- **Tree sizes:** wieldtest and daggertest take 12-30 big nodes and 1-2 ultimates (1.26 added alternates, variants,
  elements and second ultimates).
- **seatest:** the empty-ship check moves the captain past CREW_NEAR (70 m; a captain that close still mans her).
- **uitest:** a real bug. The load screen was 373 px tall on the menus' 360-high canvas, so it was scaled to 0.91 and
  its pixel fonts blurred. SaveSlotList's scroll area went 300 -> 260.
- **powertest:**
  - Infuse is bought on the Edy tree now (1.24.1: `EdyTree.learn_path("e_iron_1")`, Edy read first).
  - The red wind-up step gets a fresh grunt.
  - The ring check accepts stagger and stun.
  - **Still red:** "holding parry settles into a block (Swim)": the captain ends up in the water before that step, by
    position or timing (time-boxed; see docs/todo.md).
- **nettest five:** the guest pistol check accepts a crit.

  (PowerComponent.AUTO: hurt, low, surrounded, dodge, land, kill). Awakened (30 s): FruitForms.form says Nature for
  the fruit's powers, half the energy (PowerComponent.cost_of), cooldowns twice as fast.

  PowerComponent._fire (try_cast is split there; tests set instant_casts); FruitFX: per-fruit colours, wind-up,
  release, impact (called wherever a power lands), column (FX.light_pillar is fire's gold: it washed out every
  ultimate), the ultimate's moment, trails for moves, auras for buffs, body effects on casts. FX.fruit_skin turns arms
  or the whole body to iron or brass and restores each mesh's own material (skips EdyAura/PowerAura pieces).

  foot_k/torso_k, the clothes it bursts out of) and Humanoid.set_beast(on, fur, kind). A guest reads the form from the
  look's build.

  gust_updraft, bear_avalanche); `i_` node ids are taken (Iron's new ones are `ir_`); the light stage's ground is at
  y = 3; a power test must face the captain north right before casting (the idle state turns the model); FX.bolt skips
  a bolt whose *start* is out of the camera's burst range (draw sky bolts from the ground up); static funcs can't use
  autoloads (FruitFX reaches Net through the captain's tree); abilityshot must slot an unowned power directly (equip

## 2026-10-31: gadgets, piece 1 - the belt, the smoke pellet and the tar bomb (1.28)
- **What:** a gadget belt per captain (`scripts/gadgets/gadget_belt.gd`, `Player.gadgets`): blueprints known, gadgets
  built (tier 0-2 = Mk I-III, charges), three slots. **U** fires the selected one (`gadget_fire`; pad LB+LT in Pad.LAYER),
  **Shift+U** cycles (`gadget_cycle`, matched exactly and checked first since Shift+U also matches U; pad: the share
  button). Usable whenever `is_free()` (Idle/Move/Jump/Fall), whatever's in hand. Charges per use (refilled at a bench
  later), a cooldown after every use as a game-time timestamp (`PlayerState.now_s`), nothing per frame.
- **Numbers:** all in `scripts/gadgets/gadget_data.gd` (GadgetData.GADGETS, per-tier arrays).
- **Throw:** `gd_lob` (GadgetPoses via TechniquePoses' `gd_` prefix, upper body, release at u 0.52 of 0.42 s, the
  gadget in the left hand: its mesh's "gadget:<id>:<tier>" model meta so HumanoidSync shows it on puppets). Auto-aim: the
  foe nearest the camera's line within range (dot 0.8), else 70% of range ahead on the ground. GadgetThrow flies the arc
  (only while flying), then GadgetZone.
- **Zones** (`gadget_zone.gd`): smoke = a flip_emitter cloud (tint per tier, Mk III violet with sparkles); foes caught
  are `blinded` once (PirateGrunt.blinded: drops the swing, staggers, coughs; others `stagger` if they have it); a captain
  inside is veiled (`GadgetVeil`, autoload-free so Stealth can name it): Stealth.range_for gives 0 and the grunt's
  `_player_ok` false (no new attacks, the 4 s give-up). Tar = a glossy black decal blot; foes in it `slowed(0.5, k)` each
  0.25 s tick (only grunts have `slowed`: beasts and fauna aren't slowed yet).
- **Co-op:** the thrower runs the lob and sends `Net.event(player, "gadget", [id, tier, from, to])`; every screen flies
  its own throw and makes its own zone (visuals local), and only the host's zone touches foes (a Timer, host only). The
  pouch on the back (GadgetModels.pouch, by the belt's best tier) rides the snapshot flags (`NF_POUCH`, bits 9-10 =
  tier+1); Humanoid.pouch_tier re-wears it on a body rebuild.
- **Saved:** SaveGame "gadgets" (GadgetBelt.to_dict). **HUD:** `scripts/ui/gadget_belt_hud.gd` right of the skill bar
  (polls every 0.1 s real time, redraws on a change). **Debug menu (F4):** a Gadgets section (build any at any tier onto
  the belt, refill all, learn every blueprint).
- **Per frame/tick:** nothing while idle. While used: the HUD's 0.1 s poll; a flying throw's physics tick (~0.6 s); each
  zone's 0.25 s host timer over the "enemies" group; one CPUParticles emitter per zone.
- **Tests:** t/gadgets belt_fire, smoke, tar. Render: `abilityshot gadget:<id>:<tier>`.

## 2026-10-31: gadgets, piece 3 - traversal: grappling hook, spring boots, pocket glider, climbing spike (1.28)
- **GadgetState** (`scripts/player_states/gadget_state.gd`, state "Gadget"): not in player.tscn; GadgetBelt._ready adds
  it to the captain's StateMachine and registers it the way the machine registers its children, handing it `player`
  and `input_buffer` itself (its `_ready` is empty: PlayerState's awaits the scene owner, which a runtime node hasn't).
- **Fire:** GadgetBelt.fire asks `GadgetState.reason(p, id, tier)` first (["why not", where]); a refusal toasts and spends
  nothing. Traversal gadgets have no charges (cooldown only) and force the state with {"id", "tier", "at"}.
- **Grapple:** `hook_point` = the camera's line of sight within range, at least HOOK_ABOVE 1 m over your feet (not the
  ground ahead). A GadgetRope (rope + the hook's own model, VineRope's calls so `Player._rope_end` shows it on puppets,
  as a vine there) shoots out, then you're hauled at the tier's pull until the chest is HAUL_OVER 0.5 m over the hook,
  2.2 s, or snagged (barely moving 0.25 s), then popped up 8.5 + 4 ahead (Fall). Speed lines while hauling.
- **Spring boots:** velocity.y = the tier's jump (11/13/15) with a dust ring and a ring, squash and a camera kick (Fall).
- **Glider:** only airborne; GadgetModels.glider_wing on the torso (Mk III red with brass tips), `gd_glide`; sinks toward
  the tier's fall rate, flies ahead at its speed, the stick turns it slowly (GLIDE_TURN 0.25 of a normal turn); landing,
  jump or the tier's time ends it. Keeps freefall_from fresh (no tumble).
- **Spike:** a wall within 1.2 m of the chest (steep normal); `gd_hang`; hangs to the tier's hold, forward climbs 1.6
  m/s (hopping over the top when the wall runs out), jump kicks off up 8 and away 3. Sparks and a clang going in.
- **Poses:** GadgetPoses gd_grapple, gd_glide, gd_hang (held, blended in over their spec length; ActionSpecs "hold").
- **Open:** a crewmate sees your hook's line as a vine (the puppet's rope is VineRope); a grapple aboard a moving ship
  isn't ship-relative; the glider over water ends in a Fall once its time is up (then you swim).
- **Per tick:** only while in the state (the grapple's ray once at fire; the spike's wall ray every 0.15 s while climbing).
- **Tests:** t/gadgets grapple, spring_boots, glider, spike. Render: modelshot `GadgetModels.glider_wing(t)`,
  `GadgetModels.mesh("grapple"|"spring_boots"|"glider"|"spike", t)`.

  smoke plume, spray and splash astern, a shake aboard.

- **Smoke screen:** a cloud (one flip_emitter) laid 6 m astern now and every 2 s for its secs; `ShipGadgets.hidden(n)`
  (n within a cloud's radius while the screen lasts). EnemyShip._huntable asks it, so a hunter drops the chase (pursuers
  _lost, others PATROL) and won't take it up in the smoke; once she's out of it (or it's over) she can be found again.
- **Harpoon cannon** (`scripts/ship/harpoon_cannon.gd`, HarpoonCannon): the contract is in docs/gadgets_plan.md
  "Harpoon contract". The line is a GadgetRope (new `thick`, 3.5x) with the harpoon head; EnemyShip got
  `harpooned_by`, `harpooned`, `released`, `reel_toward`. The bite is a `siege` hit (hulls only take those).
- **Bench:** the list scrolls now (20 gadgets; LIST_H 300).
- **Per frame/tick:** a harpoon's physics tick only while its line is out; Ship one compare (paddle_t); each smoke cloud
  a CPUParticles emitter while it lasts (up to ~9 at Mk III); `hidden()` is called by hunting enemy ships each tick
  (returns at once with no clouds).
- **Tests:** t/ship burst_launcher, smoke_screen, harpoon_cannon. Render: `tools/dev/shipgadgetshot.gd <out> [tier]`.
## 1.28: the volcanic isle, piece 1 (the land, lava flows, plants, textures) (2026-10-31)
- **What:** a new island theme, `volcanic` (docs/volcanic_island_plan.md), registered in IslandThemes.SCRIPTS. Rolled
  apart like the fog isle (weight 0.22) and only from the chain's fourth layer on (new `ThemeDef.from_layer`, read by
  `Chain._apart`; every other island of every chain stays as it was, and the smoketest's first islands can't roll it).
- **Land** (`scripts/island/themes/volcanic_land.gd`): one cone near the middle (rim 70-95 m, lower on small islands so
  the gully stays walkable: h <= foot x 0.42), a caldera floor 25-33 m under the rim, the rim breached toward the
  village by a gully at an even grade (lerped to `_ramp` within BREACH_W of the axis). New hook `ThemeDef.site_at(isl,
  site, p)` (GenIsland._plan_sites, themes with a land plan): the boss's ground is the caldera's floor, the summit's
  lookout on the rim beside the breach, camp/lair/ruins pushed to the cone's foot and off the gully; `village_at` puts
  the town past the foot. Gotcha: the cone's "land" factor is by distance from the coast (`_coast_t`), not the base's
  height: smoothstep(0.5, 4, h) wavered with the base's noise on this low island and put 1-2 m steps in the flanks.
  The bearing-cliff tear under the middle is taken out as on the snow's peak.
- **Lava flows:** 3-5 channels with levees from side vents to near the foot (a distance grid with the nearest flow's
  index, `flow_near`). Hot stretches (one emissive flow-shader mesh, no lights) except: a flow aimed at the breach,
  near the village or dock (55 m), where a path crosses (4.5 m), on a place's or cave's ground, and the last segments
  (a cooled lobe): those are basalt crust. A crescent of lava in the caldera's back (for the salamander, piece 5).
  `volcanic_hazard.gd`: 5 Hz, the local captain in hot lava takes 15 and is thrown 7 m/s out and 9 up (0.8 s grace);
  embers/sfx through Net.fx; one distance check while off the island. The plume: 14 CPU puffs high over the caldera
  (seen to 1600 m), 10 embers over the crescent.
- **Plants** (`scripts/props/volcanic_plants.gd`, VolcanicPlants): charred trees (an ember glowing in a split), ash
  pines (ForestPlants._tier tiers), scorched giants and great pines (few: canopy 0.18), ash shrubs, fire lilies, wiry ash
  grass, fumaroles, pumice, basalt and obsidian rocks. Five forests (ash barrens, scorched woods, cinder fields, ash
  pine slopes, fumarole flats).
- **Style:** stone and dark timber houses under `volcanic_slate`, cinder paving, orange lamps, ash/black sand/cinder/
  basalt ground; its text (volcanic_life.gd: smiths, tinkers, quarrymen, ash farmers, fire-keepers) and encounters.
  Placeholders until their pieces: music desert_night/desert_town_night, ambience desert, beasts reused (basilisk and
  serpent as bosses, alpha boar, behemoth), fauna from the shared roster (monitor lizards, scorpions, crabs...).
- **Textures:** `tools/texture_gen/gen_volcanic_textures.py` (volcanic_ash, _sand, _cinder, _basalt, _lava, _slate,
  _grass, _lily).
- **Tests:** t/island/volcanic_land (three islands; the burn on the light stage). Render: genshot chain seed 2 node 6
  (`genshot.gd -- <out> 2 6`). Per tick: the hazard's 5 Hz check (a distance test off the island); no new lights.

## 1.28: the volcanic isle, piece 2 (the forge town) (2026-10-31)
- **The smiths' yard** (`scripts/island/themes/volcanic_town.gd`, a theme place `volcanic_forge` through
  VolcanicTheme.plan_places / place_steps): 70-110 m out of the village toward the mountain, flat, off the flows (a trail
  run to it by KitLandmarks). An open slate shed over the great forge (a basalt hearth with a lava trough: the flow
  shader, one light from the budget), a smoking brick chimney, bellows, two anvils each with a smith (`volcanic_anvil.gd`:
  the anvil takes and a spit of embers every ~1.3 s of game time while the captain is within 45 m; local ambience),

  "Teach me a blueprint (price gold)" teaches the first blueprint in his order (shuffled per island) that the captain
  doesn't know (`Gadgets.teach`), paid only when one's learned; without the gold or with nothing left, "Come back...".
  His answer is a dialogue token filled as the line shows (the event fires before the page). Price 120 + 60 x tier.

  dressed as shelves (KitShops.KINDS gained "parts"; desert_shops' count now follows the list).

## 1.28: the volcanic isle, piece 4 (rumbles and bursts) (2026-10-31)
- **What** (`scripts/island/themes/volcanic_eruptions.gd`, a VolcanicLand step): while a captain is on or near the
  island (radius + 120 m), the host sets an eruption off every 150-260 s (the first 45-70 s after arriving; gaps from
  the island's seed and the eruption's number) and sends only its number (`Net.event(self, "erupt", [n])`). Every
  machine then plays the same eruption from the seed and n (`plan(n)`): a camera shake and the volcano's rumble
  (`volcano_rumble.wav`), embers and dust bursting from the caldera, then after 2.2 s 10-16 lava bombs over 6 s in one
  sector (a seeded point 0.3-0.7 of the radius out, kept 90 m off the village and the dock, every bomb 60 m off them).
  Each bomb: a warning 1.6 s ahead (the shared telegraph, plus a red circle laid on the ground with a bright rim and a
  fill growing to it: the flat telegraph sank into slopes), the bomb falling in a glowing arc for its last 0.8 s, then
  embers, dust and the `lava_bomb` sound (FX.SOUNDS). It hurts only inside its 3 m circle (22, thrown out), each
  machine only its own captain. A late joiner picks up the next number from the host's event.
- **Sounds:** `tools/texture_gen/gen_volcanic_audio.py` (volcano_rumble, lava_bomb_1/2, and the bed volcanic_loop).
- **Tests:** t/island/volcanic_eruptions (plans the same from the same number, sectors clear of the town, red circles
  before landing, a captain on a bomb's spot burned and one clear of them not, the host's count, a guest following it).
  Render: `tools/dev/volcanoshot.gd -- <out> 2 6` (genshot's shots plus the eruption from over its sector).
- Per tick: one countdown a second on the host; the bomb queue only during an eruption.

## 1.28: the volcanic isle, piece 5 (the magma salamander) (2026-10-31)

  paddle tail. **On the beast pass** (`_pass_moves`), so its fight erupts in phases (at 2/3 and 1/3 health: the moment,

  nobody bumps it: `Net.event(self, "under")` on every screen), swims at its quarry for 2.4 s leaving a wake of embers
  and dust (Net.fx), stops 3 m short, lays a red ring where the captain stands (0.9 s), then bursts up through it
  (28, its one knockdown), back in sight. (Rising at the captain's feet: `ground_at` from 6 m up hit a dressing
  collider and stood it on top of them.)

  basalt spires and boulders with black glass round the edge on the way in's sides, the back left open to the lava
  crescent, glowing cracks across the floor, charred bones. Its banner: "The Caldera".

## 2026-11-01: the rapier, piece 1 (1.28 weapons; docs/v1_28_plan.md "Weapons", docs/weapons_126.md)
- **Its own kind now** (WeaponDesigns "rapier", base resources/items/rapier.tres, id "rapier": the cutlass's old "rapier"
  design moved here, so a saved rapier is the new kind; the cutlass has one design fewer). `_rapier`: grip at the origin,
  quillons across Y, a knuckle bow round to the pommel, a square ricasso and a long needle of a blade (`_blade`, taper
  0.5); hilts "cup" (a steel bowl), "swept" (side rings, bars round the hand), "shell" (two shell plates). Designs: swept
  rapier, smallsword (short, "speed" 1.1), colichemarde (a broad "forte" third), flamberge ("wave" blade, "bleed" 3 s),
  quicksilver (RARE: a glowing mercury edge), gilded (skin). `WeaponDesigns.rapier(design, key)`: speed, reach, bleed.
  One-handed but takes no off hand (Player.style_of / _offhand_valid): the free hand fences. Worn on the hip.
- **Moveset** (style and stance "rapier"; RapierMoves keyed poses written as directions: "arm" / "fore" / "blade" in the
  root's frame, solved in the chest's frame (`_aim`), the wrist kept steady where the blade runs along the forearm and
  written the short way round (`_wrist`) so keys blend through the line, not round the side). Guard side on (StanceLife.HIPS
  0.75), the point at their eyes, the free hand up behind. Combo rp_1 the straight thrust on an advance / rp_2 the
  disengage into the high line / rp_3 the phantom double (the mirror's thrust leaves a silver afterimage, a snap back, the
  real thrust on a lunge 0.2 s later: LightAttackState "phantoms" re-arms the hitbox at RapierMoves.PHANTOM_AT[1], 16
  finisher). Heavy **the Lunge** (HeavyAttackState "lunge", rp_heavy: sunk back, a breath, then 13 m/s into a deep lunge,
  REACH "rapier_lunge" 4.1 m, a breaker that reels them, not a knockdown). **Parry-riposte**: the parry turns the wrist
  (rp_parry); a landed one plays rp_deflect and RIPOSTE_DELAY 0.16 s later `RapierArts.riposte` puts the point into the
  attacker within 3.2 m: 16 finisher, a sure crit, unblockable, stagger 0.8, a step in. The Fleche (rp_dash) is wired for
  a sprint's attack behind move "fleche" (the tree, piece 2). REACH "rapier" 2.9 m deep, x the design's reach.
- **Colours** FX.TREE_FX "rapier" quicksilver mirror: silver-white core, mercury grey-blue edge, a warm mirror-flash
  accent. `FX.quicksilver` (mercury beads, a mirror glint) for element / elem_hit; `FX.mirror_thrust` (the thrust's line and
  its fainter mirror double a hand to the side, a stretched star glint at the point). Without the element: plain steel
  rings and glints at the point, the afterimages in plain white.
- **Sources**: a chest that keeps a cutlass or dagger makes it a rapier RAPIER_CHANCE 0.15 (hoard 0.3) from its own stream
  (`|rapier`); Haldor's pool rapier / smallsword / swept_rapier@1 / colichemarde@1; Shops.RARE_KINDS; WeaponDesigns
  .random_item; story rack (Vey's) and Shift+F10's rack. Traits: gale, bloodthirsty, rushing, duellist's.
- **Co-op**: nothing new on the wire (the stance, actions and model sync; hits through hurtboxes, effects through Net.fx;
  the riposte runs on the parrying captain's machine like black-leg's sweep).
- **Per frame/tick**: nothing new (keyed poses; a timer for the riposte).
- Tests: t/weapons/rapier_combo, rapier_riposte; qoltest's legendary-design check now uses the swept rapier. Renders:
  tools/dev/out/rp_side_*, rp_front_* (animsheet), rp_models_sheet, rp_hilt_* (modelshot). posebench doesn't compile on
  main right now (scripts/gadgets/gadget_belt.gd:89 names FX in a static context: the gadgets agent's). Expect the chest-roll
  suites, Haldor's stock, the cutlass's design count and the story rack to want a look at the push.

## 1.28 sea stops, piece 1: the stop roll and the wandering merchant (2026-11-01, docs/v1_28_plan.md "The sea")
- **The roll:** `Chain.sea_stop(from, to, tier)` from its own stream (hash of the chain seed and the leg): chance by the
  destination's layer `STOP_CHANCE` (0 on layers 1-2, 0.22 at 3 up to 0.58 at 9), kinds `STOP_KINDS` weighted
  `STOP_WEIGHTS` [restaurant 3, merchant 4, warlord 2, lieutenant 1 + 1.2 per bounty tier]. Over 60 chains: none
  early, ~29% of mid legs, ~55% of late ones. `SeaStops.kind_for` passes the crew's hottest bounty tier (bounties ride
  in the captains' snapshots, so screens agree unless a bounty tier changes while a leg is being laid out: known
  edge); `SeaStops.force` makes every leg have one (debug, tests).
- **Placing:** `SeaLegs.plan` adds "stop"/"stop_at" after everything else from its own rng (every existing leg's
  layout is unchanged), on open water 30-75% along the leg within LANE 160 m of the route (`_spot`, room 70 m);
  `_build_leg` builds it (`SeaStops.build`, node "Stop", seed = leg seed + 77) and puts it in EnemyShip.no_go.
- **SeaVessel** (scripts/sea/sea_vessel.gd): the floating stops' base: its own sailing like EnemyShip (`_pos`/`_heading`,
  `place()`), the swell, group "decks" (aboard by a ship-local `bounds` AABB, deck_delta, hull_velocity), net_sync
  (host sails; guests ease onto its snapshots: [pos, heading, speed, yaw rate, net_extra()]), ActorSleep SHIP radii.
- **MerchantShip** (scripts/sea/merchant_ship.gd): TraderShips.merchantman's three-master with a striped awning, crates
  and bales on deck, ladders both sides. Sails a slow round (CRUISE 3.5 m/s, ROUND_R 90) about her spot; heaves to
  and hails (a bark, the bell) when the crew's ship is within HAIL_R 130 with a captain aboard, or a captain within
  SWIM_R 60; sails on WAIT 30 s after nobody's near or aboard. Her factor (NPC, a shop) trades from Shops.extra
  "merchant_<seed>": a fine weapon (tier + 1, with a trait), two rare gear pieces, two blueprints, three parts, two
  exotic ingredients, and `MerchantShip.book_pool` (empty: the books agent fills it, BOOKS_SHOWN 2). Rerolled per
  visit (each leg's merchant is a new seed). Two scenery deckhands.
- **F4:** "Sea stop: <kind>" in the spawn list (`SeaStops.debug_spawn`: ~60 m ahead on the water; host only, not
  mirrored to guests). Kinds not built yet spawn nothing.
- Per tick: one merchant at most per standing leg: its sailing and swell (5 wave samples), 3 humanoids (LOD), no
  test_move; asleep past 420 m. Cargo mesh: one surface set, visibility 260 m, no shadow.
- Tests: `t/sea/stop_rolls`, `t/sea/merchant`. legtest (world suite) maps to sea_legs.gd: expect it at prepush.

  cook-off table (`FloatingRestaurant.cookoff`: a Callable the cooking timing game sets; unset, the chef says it's
  not on). Four seated diners and the cook-off judge (scenery) when she's not raided.

  bouillabaisse free (`_favour`: banner, bell) and the chef's lines change.
- Per tick: nothing moves; a 1 s poll for the raid; NPCs (up to 6) sleep past 160 m like villagers.

## 1.28 sea stops, piece 3: the big named ships (2026-11-01)
- **BigShip** (scripts/sea/big_ship.gd) extends EnemyShip: new KINDS "flagship" (a warlord's: black hull, crimson sails,
  1300 hull) and "warship" (an Admiralty lieutenant's: white and blue, 1400 hull, a bow chaser; in ADMIRALTY_KINDS),
  both four guns a side with double broadsides, never boarding or ramming. Drawn K 1.5 times as big by scaling the body
  in `_place_hull` (the model, collision, guns, ladders, hurtbox and the swell all follow; Jolt takes the uniform
  scale): ~34 m long, her deck about level with ours. Her men are scaled back (1/K) and set back to 1 when they turn
  grunt (`_turn_grunt`). Title over her: "<ship> (<captain>)".
- **Cannons, board, duel:** she comes for the crew whatever their bounty (`_wants_crew`), trades broadsides at 34-64 m;
  under BATTERED_AT 75% hull her rigging's shot through (a bark) and she can't make more than 2.5 m/s, so the crew can
  come alongside. Board by her ladders or "Swing aboard" (an Interactable each side, 7 m round a spot off her rail,
  usable from a deck alongside or the water: lands you inside her rail with a rope tracer). Her crew of eight turns to
  fight on her deck (EnemyShip's DECK); with CAPTAIN_AT 2 or fewer up, or CAPTAIN_AFTER 25 s, her captain (an AI
  captain via Net._all_spawn_rival / RivalDuel.build on the quarterdeck; health x CAPTAIN_HP 3.5 + level x 0.05,
  elite poise, pace 1.2, skill 0.75 / 0.85, a weapon by kind) is introduced by a cutscene on every screen (Cutscene
  kind "sea_captain": `BigShip.intro_shots`) and duels the nearest boarder. Beaten (`defeated`), the captain yields
  (a bark), is gone 2.5 s later (`_all_rival_gone`) and she strikes: XP 500 (reach 200), bounty x BOUNTY_K 3 (4,500
  for the warlord's, 3,000 for the lieutenant's), the captain's chest on her quarterdeck (gold 160-260, treasure,
  rum, a tier+1 weapon, a gear piece, a blueprint, parts, salvage), and a "prize" Net.event for guests.
- **Sunk from afar:** `_drop_chest` leaves only salvage (no flotsam chest): the hoard goes down with her.
- **Fleeing:** as any EnemyShip (lost past LOSE 240 m).
- **Rolls:** Chain.sea_stop's "warlord" / "lieutenant" -> SeaStops builds a "StopWarm" (scripts/sea/stop_warm.gd) that
  prebuilds her crew's bodies on a worker thread and then makes her (`SeaStops.big`, node "Stop" on the leg,
  patrolling 70 m about the spot). The lieutenant's weight grows with the crew's bounty tier (piece 1).
- Seen in passing: EnemyShip._bounty_kind has a `Net.event(self, "prize", [])` after its return (dead code), so a
  guest never runs `_prize` for an ordinary prize; BigShip sends its own event. Not fixed here.
- Per tick: as an EnemyShip (asleep past 420 m on patrol); the captain is one AI Player only during the duel.
- Tests: `t/sea/big_ship` (scale, her men's size, she hunts, battered she loses way, a captain on her deck stands, her

## 2026-11-01 Cooking pieces B and C: island dishes, crew feasts, the cook-off (1.28 life systems)
- **Island dishes:** each theme's own ingredient (`Food.STAPLES`: fire chili, frost berries, desert dates, black truffle,
  ghost lily, ember salt, sea grapes for the atoll) is always in that island's village cookpot (`Shops.STAPLE_PRICE`,
  added in IslandVillage's cookpot stock) and the grocer pools grew fog / volcanic / atoll lists. Two dishes a theme
  (14, the plan's table + two atoll ones), known from the start, in the galley's (now scrolling) list.
- **Recipes by item id:** a recipe key is a tag, `"island"` (any staple) or an exact item id (`Food.fits`). `Food.picks`
  fills exact items first, then "island", then tags, and tracks what it's taken, so Truffle Risotto's "greens" never
  eats the truffle the dish is named for. `Food.tag_name` reads keys (the ingredient's own name for an id).

  crew's ship (`Food.aboard`, `can_cook` refuses ashore). Served, `Net.everyone("_all_feast")` feeds every captain
  aboard at the cook's strength x grade (banner), the cook's portion included; extra portions go on the galley table.
- **Cook-off** at the floating restaurant (`FloatingRestaurant._cook_off`, replaces the `cookoff` Callable hook): once a
  visit per captain, the judge names one of the day's dishes, the cooking game at x1.15 speed, no ingredients;
  prizes by grade (`COOKOFF`: 0/40/120/300 gold, XP, 3 of a staple on Good, A Cook's Atlas on Perfect). A raided
  restaurant's table waits until the raiders are beaten.

## 2026-11-01 The temple crash: the Edy reading's tokens
- Zach's game died as Master Isao read his Edy. Every Progression's `_ready` registered `{edy_read}` / `{edy_says}` /
  `{edy_price}` as lambdas bound to itself, the last one winning; AI captains (rivals, officers) have a Progression too,

  type's attunement in a window (no GPU fault there). Test: `t/story/edy_tokens`.

## 1.28: the coral atoll (2026-11-02)
- **What:** a new island theme, `atoll` (docs/v1_28_plan.md "Islands"), registered last in IslandThemes.SCRIPTS. Rolled
  apart like the fog and volcanic isles (weight 0.2, from the chain's second layer). Every number is in
  `scripts/island/themes/atoll_data.gd`. Landed in five pieces (land/town, places/life, beasts, boss, sound).
- **Land** (`atoll_land.gd`): the base coast becomes the sea edge of a ring 48-64 m wide (wobbling by bearing); along it
  islets (crest 2.2-3.6 m, palm-grown) alternate with sandbars (-0.5 m floor, -0.18 crest: wading), cut by 1-2 passes
  (-2.8 m, a swim; never by the dock or village). Outside: a 14 m reef flat at -1.1 m, then the drop-off to -30 over 22 m
  (where DiveSites' own spots land). Inside: the lagoon at -2.5..-3.1 (deeper than SpearSchool.DEEP_M 2.5 over most of
  it), coral heads (cellular noise) up to -0.7, 2-4 lagoon islets (motu; the first big, 58-70 m, kept for the caves),
  a blue hole 13-17 m deep. The village sits on the ring beside the dock on its own widened islet (70 m, 2.5 m high:
  VillageLayouts wants ground over 2 m); the boss's tidal flat is in the lagoon away from the village (the base land's
  low 0.9 m, restored by the sites' kept land), a wading causeway out to it with 1-2 swims. Hooks: new
  `ThemeDef.route(isl, site, pts)` (GenIsland._define_paths: the atoll's paths run round the ring at its middle and down
  the causeway); `site_at(isl, "cave", p)` (KitDungeons._plan_cave, land-plan themes only: the atoll's caves go on the
  big motu; others return p unchanged). The theme's plan_places appends the big motu to `avoid` so landmarks keep off it.
  Gotcha: shape() returns the base height until the dock is placed (the dock's search walks out from the middle).
- **Town:** the village's style rolls the stilts layout mostly (woven/bamboo houses on stilts, palm thatch, torches),
  harbour kinds stilts/cove/wharf. `atoll_town.gd` (theme place "atoll_stilts"): a boardwalk on palm piles from the
  village's lagoon shore out over the water (turned 0.3-0.6 rad off the causeway), 5-8 huts on piles off spurs, the
  square (two stalls, net rack, traps, lamps from the budget), fishing platforms; the pearl trader (Shops.extra
  `isleN_pearl_trader`: pearls, oysters, urchins, seaweed; buys loot x1.15), two fishers, a net-mender.
- **Places** (`atoll_places.gd`, the chain's set pieces mapped): a trader wrecked on the reef flat (HullBuilder wreck x1.25,
  a chest aboard, one sunk at her stern, wreckers camped on the islet above: GruntCamp + nav zone), a pearl bed in the
  shallows (4-6 DiveSites.oyster_bed, the divers' raft, buoys, a diver), the blue hole dressed (coral gardens round its
  lip, DiveSites.sunken_ruin and a sunken chest on its floor). Opened chests and taken oysters stay gone per save.
- **Fishing hooks** (`atoll_spots.gd`, AtollSpots): Marker3Ds in group `fishing_spots` (kind "line") or `spear_spots`
  (kind "spear"), metadata kind/where/depth/r/theme "atoll": the passes' mouths, the blue hole (both), coral heads'
  feet (spear, >2.5 m), the drop-off off the dock's islets, the boss flat's edge; the town's platforms ("pier") under
  Place_atoll_stilts/Spots; the wreck and pearl bed (spear). `AtollSpots.list(isl)` gives the same as data.
- **Life:** `atoll_shoals.gd` + `shaders/atoll_shoal.gdshader`: 6-10 fish shoals circling under the lagoon (a MultiMesh of
  18-30 each, turned on the GPU, ranged 120 m, unshadowed) and 3 gull flocks wheeling over it (500 m): no CPU a frame.
  Roster: shore crabs (dense), coconut crabs (Crab, morph 1, bigger), boobies in the palm crowns (Toucan's perch slot:
  roster key "toucan" -> atoll_booby.gd), monitor lizards, sea snakes, bats in caves. Plants (AtollPlants): coconut
  palms, tall palms, screw pines, salt scrub, spider lilies, beach grass, sprouts, coral rubble, driftwood, coral rocks.
  Textures gen_atoll_textures.py (atoll_sand/_turf/_coral/_seafloor/_grass/_lily/_seagrass).
- **Beasts** (move tables, the tell language from alpha_boar's table): the salt croc (mini at the lair: bite to parry,
  tail, lunge = its knockdown, death roll in phase 2) and the Tidemaw roamer (a coral-crusted sea turtle on the
  behemoth's wander: snap, wash, shell bash, water spouts).
- **Boss** (`atoll_hermit.gd`, on the beast pass, its own body on alpha_boar's table brain): shell hits chip shell HP
  (900) and reach the crab x0.35; cracked off, the body takes x1.6; hurt 18% bare it scuttles straight to one of three
  spare shells round its post (deterministic from post/yaw), hides 3.2 s (hurtbox off, +4% health), bursts out (a ring)
  wearing it (each 0.8x thinner); out of spares it fights bare. Phases 0.66/0.33: pinch (parry), crush, spit | sweep,
  charge (knockdown) | spin. Co-op: shell/hidden/spares used ride its snapshot (_pack_extra). The flat is dressed by
  `AtollTheme._dress_flat` (tide pools, leg furrows, smashed shell, driftwood).
- **Sound:** gen_atoll_music.py (atoll 88 bpm G mixolydian: marimba, steel drum, congas, ocarina; atoll_town 108 bpm C:
  guitar, steel drum and tin whistle, clave; night versions on the same form), gen_atoll_audio.py (atoll_loop: lagoon
  lap, far surf, palm rustle, gulls and terns). Music.TRACKS, Ambience.LOOPS/TOP_DB lines.

## 2026-11-02: the skimmer and the gadget bag (1.28.1 gadgets)
- **The skimmer** (`scripts/player_states/skimmer_state.gd`, `scripts/gadgets/skimmer_model.gd`; data in GadgetData
  "skimmer", numbers in docs/gadgets_plan.md): an atoll-only traversal gadget, a windsurfing board. U launches it from
  the shore's edge or the ship's side (SkimmerState.launch_point: water >= 0.8 m deep 2-6.5 m ahead, a clear line to it;
  a 0.45 s hop out onto it) or right where you swim. The "Skimmer" state is added to the captain's state machine at
  runtime by GadgetBelt, like "Gadget". WASD steers camera-relative (TURN 2.6 rad/s); held, it runs up to the tier's
  9/11/13 m/s times `wind_k` (Weather.wind_dir against the heading: beam 1.0, running 0.8, into it 0.45, by the wind's
  strength 0.85-1.0), let go it eases to COAST 0.35 of that. The board floats on `player.water_surface()` (the
  wave clock), the body aligned to the wave normal banked into turns (Player.align_up/align_hold), the rig raked by the
  turn. Mk III hops on Space (7 m/s). A blow (Player._on_hit_received), running into a wall (a slide normal within 45
  degrees of level faster than 2.5 m/s) or aground (< 0.3 m under it twice in a row) throws you into Swim; F stows it.
  The captain stands side-on (the model yawed -90 degrees off the board's heading), the gd_skim pose (GadgetPoses).
- **Its parts** (GadgetData.PARTS, ATOLL_PARTS; icons in GadgetModels.part_mesh): coral_spar, sea_silk, lagoon_pearl;
  bp_skimmer. Kept out of `Gadgets.blueprint_ids()` and `part_ids()` (the tinkerer's order, the merchant, big ships
  and chests roll from those): a gadget with a "region" key is placed by its region (the lead's atoll pass places all
  four). `Gadgets.all_blueprint_ids()` has it (items, teach, study, the debug menu). Mk I 80g + 4 spar, 2 silk, 1 pearl;
  Mk III totals 9 pearls, more than one atoll's 8.
- **The gadget bag** (`scripts/gadgets/gadget_bag.gd`, `scripts/ui/gadget_wheel.gd`): the belt alone now carries one
  gadget (GadgetData.SLOTS 1); carrying a bag item (`gadget_bag_<mustard|olive|oxblood|navy>`) six (BAG_SLOTS).
  GadgetBelt.fit() sizes the slots to what's carried on every inventory change: shrinking keeps the first filled ones,
  growing takes up the built gadgets that were off the slots. Gadgets off the slots stay built (owned), at their tier
  and charges. **Migration:** a 1.28 save's three slots go through the same fit() on load: the first filled one stays,
  the rest wait (a toast says so) and come back with a bag. O is GadgetWheel's (a RadialWheel, tap_ok): a tap
  GadgetBelt.cycle() (no bag: "A gadget bag lets you carry more"; at the helm the ship gadgets as before), held with a
  bag and two or more gadgets the wheel (entries are gadget ids). The old O handler in Player._unhandled_input is gone.
- **Getting it:** the forge town's master tinkerer (volcanic_tinkerer.gd: "A gadget bag. (250 gold)", then a colour;
  `Gadgets.buy_bag`), and hoards (Gadgets.chest_extras: 6% for a captain without one, a random colour, rolled last
  on the chest's own stream).
- **The look:** a strap tube over the right shoulder, across the chest and the back to the left hip (on the torso),
  and the sack on a three-point SpringChains chain at the left hip (skinned loft, a darker patch; its own thigh_l
  capsule keeps it off the leg), added to the body's `_sims` so it swings only within SIMS_R of the camera like hair
  and coats. The flap is a mesh on a BoneAttachment3D on the sack's top bone, tweened open (FLAP_OPEN, the gadgets in
  the mouth shown) while the wheel is up and OPEN_SECS after a pick; clasped otherwise. Humanoid.bag_colour/bag_open
  wear it again on a rebuild (apply_look), like the pouch.
- **Co-op:** a crewmate's screen builds the board on the puppet's lean node from NF_SKIM (the tier) and draws its
  spray and wake from the snapshot velocity (SkimmerModel.puppet_fx); the bag from NF_BAG (colour index) and
  NF_BAG_OPEN. Not nettested (no nettest in the build tier).
- **Per frame/tick added:** riding: one physics tick of steering, a wave height and normal, a move_and_slide, a depth ray
  every 3 ticks, spray + Ocean.wake every 0.08 s; a riding puppet the same spray/wake timer. The bag: one 2-segment
  spring chain per captain inside the body's sims radius; nothing when it's still far. No new lights; the board and rig
  have visibility ranges (120/160 m), the bag's parts 40 m and no shadows.
- **Tests:** t/gadgets skimmer_parts, skimmer_ride, bag_slots, bag_migration, bag_buy; belt_fire now carries a bag; the
  decoy test's Mk III burst is placed right by the grunt (under load he'd walked out of a burst 1 m off). Renders:
  `skimmershot` (each tier riding, side/front/back), `bagshot` (four colours, open, running).

## 2026-11-02: the hull layout as data (1.29 'Shipshape', piece 1)
- **HullLayout** (`scripts/ship/hull_layout.gd`): HullBuilder's old constants (the quarterdeck, the cabin's walls, door
  and floor, stairs, wheel/helm, mast, yard, nest, rigging, ladders) plus the gun spots and the cabin's fittings
  (bed, stove, counter, storage, table) are fields of a layout object. `HullLayout.base()` is the pirates', traders' and
  wrecks' hull (the old numbers, frozen); `HullLayout.of(class, tier)` / `for_kit(kit)` the crew's ship (class and the
  coming Quarters level, cached). The hull's shape (RINGS, DECK_Y, FREEBOARD, BOW_Z, STERN_Z, HALF_BEAM) stays as
  HullLayout consts too: const contexts (ShipSpray, Ship.DECK_Y, EnemyShip.FREEBOARD) still need them, and every crew
  class shares the hull form in 1.29. Helpers moved onto the layout: half_width, ring_at, side_at, aboard_local,
  in_cabin, nest_rail(_at); a new `cabin_y` (the cabin floor) for the stepped-down cabin.
- HullBuilder draws a layout: `hull(mb, m, rig, L)`, `collide(body, rig, L)`, `build(parent, {"layout": L})`; all
  default to base(). Ship has `layout` (set in _ready from the kit) and passes it to hull, collide, ShipLights.crew,
  ShipRigging.layout, LashedHelm; ShipParts reads `ship.layout` (its old consts RUDDER_AT, ROPE_LENGTH, COPPER_Z,
  HOOD_Y, GROVE_AT are funcs now). Ship.BED_AT etc. and GUN_SPOTS are `ship.layout.bed_at`, `.gun_spots`
  (Downtime, Progression's bunk respec, tests). Everything else (islands, birds, merchants, enemies, wrecks) reads
  `HullLayout.base()`. EnemyShip.CREW_SPOTS is a static var (it reads base()).
- **Gotcha:** HullLayout must not reference project classes that touch autoloads (no ShipClasses/ShipLines): tests
  name it statically before the autoloads load (blocked_furls failed on Settings via ShipLines). `for_kit` reads the
  kit's plain keys.
- Proof: `t/ship/layout_parity` fingerprints every vertex of the pirates' model, its collision shapes, a wreck, and the
  crew's whole sloop (meshes and shapes) against prints taken from the constants before the change: all identical.
  riggingtest, looptest, yard_ropes, bigshipshot read `ship.layout` (their `HB` is the layout now, lowercase fields).

## 2026-11-02: the sloop reworked (1.29 'Shipshape', piece 2)
- **The cabin stepped down and bigger**: every crew class's layout (`HullLayout._crew`, tier 0) has the cabin floor
  `cabin_y` 0.4 m under the main deck and the quarterdeck from 4.4 (was 5.0; stairs from 0.9). HullBuilder splits the
  hull at `qd_front` (`_segments`: the stern castle aft of it, the waist forward), lays the castle's floor at
  `cabin_y`, stands the cabin walls on it (the lintel from the deck), and for a stepped cabin adds a sill and
  `step_count` steps of `STEP_RUN` inside the door and closes the corners between the front wall and the hull
  (`_cabin_steps`). Collision: the hull volume in two (deck height forward, floor height under the cabin) and a ramp
  over the steps. The pirates' base() hull is unchanged (layout_parity's fingerprints still match).
- **Ship builds by layout**: `_build_layout()` puts the hull mesh, the cabin (ShipCabin), the helm (ShipWheel), the
  lanterns, the cabin zones, seats, workbench and bookshelf under `ShipModel/Layout`, the ladders and the galley table
  by name on ShipModel (tests use those paths), its collision shapes in `_layout_shapes`, and sets the helm marker, helm
  zone and respawn point from the layout. `_relayout()` (apply_kit, when `HullLayout.for_kit` changes) frees all that
  and builds it again, moves the quarterdeck guns, drops the mizzen and the helm lashing to be rebuilt, and forces
  ShipParts to rebuild. The storage chests are built once (`_build_storage`) and moved.
- **ShipCabin** (`scripts/ship/ship_cabin.gd`): the furnished room per Quarters level (tier 0 here: bunk with a shelf,
  stove and counter with pots, crates round the chest, table and stools, small stern windows, a lantern), `solids()`
  and `seats()` for it. Two meshes (Cabin, CabinFine at 14 m); `_show_cabin` hides both and the cabin light unless the
  camera is in or near the cabin (checked 4x a second).
- **Ladders** (`Ladder.lean`, `rung_at`, `hold_at`): the hull ladders lie on the hull as it tucks in (lean from the ring
  at ladder_z, ~0.69 m in per metre down) and end at the waterline (`ladder_len` = deck + freeboard + 0.06, was 3.0);
  ClimbState follows `hold_at`. The pirates' and docks' ladders are unchanged (lean 0).
- **The flag** (`_build_flag`): a pole on the masthead with a gilt truck, the flag hoisted along it in six rippled,
  sagging panels (both faces read), on `_flag_pivot`, which turns downwind with a slow stir each frame (`_show_flag`:
  PI - the wind's bearing) and goes up 0.75 over the nest's hood (`raise_flag`, ShipParts).
- **The wheel** (`ShipWheel`, `scripts/ship/ship_wheel.gd`): eight spokes through an inner ring, a twelve-felloe rim,
  turned handles, a hub with the axle's end, on a turned post with an axle box (the old post was a plank). `fit_helm(n)`
  builds both at a Rudder & helm level (levels shown from piece 3).
- Per frame added: `_show_flag` (one lerp_angle) and `_show_cabin` (a timer; a to_local 4x a second).
- Tests: t/ship/cabin_step (in the door and down the steps onto the cabin floor, the bunk/galley/chest prompts, the
  respawn by the bunk, back up and out), t/ship/hull_ladder (ends at the waterline, rungs on the hull, down into the sea
  and back up), layout_parity's WANT_SHIP renewed; t/downtime/sleep gets up on the cabin floor. riggingtest's cabin
  check reads `cabin_y`. Renders: bigshipshot BSHOT_ONLY / BSHOT_KIT and the shots cabin_wide, cabin_aft, cabin_steps,
  helm, flag, ladder_side (tools/dev/out/shipshape/p2_*).

## 2026-11-04: Redtide's mountain (1.30, piece 1: the shape)
- **What:** Morrow's arena now sits in the bowl of a mountain rising from the sea instead of on a lone stack.
  `RedtideFort._build_massif` (redtide_fort.gd): a horseshoe massif on a polar grid round the arena (120 columns
  over every bearing but the cove's, OPEN_A +Z = toward Brinehollow, OPEN_HALF 0.9 rad), each column a profile
  (`_col` / `_profile`): the inner foot buried under the arena rock's rim (19 m, so no gap opens), a sheer inner
  wall with two shelves, the crest (22 m + 26 m at the back, PEAKS, ridge noise; 15 m min, the arms' tips 30% lower),
  a rolling top (wide on the arms), a sheer outer cliff with a steep (>50 deg) ledge band, a sea notch, the apron
  down to -36. The arms hook in round the cove (`_bent`, 0.24 rad at their tips) and end in sheer caps
  (the profile triangulated). Facets with true normals as the stack; grass on flats (noise-gated), a mossy ledge
  rock, a warmer rock tint. One trimesh. Crest spires (CREST) and sea stacks off the foot (CRAGS, by gap past the
  foot; MOUTH out past the cove) replace the old crags; the waterline boulders only in the cove.
- **The one way in:** the cove, the jetty and the stair are unchanged in place; everything else is sheer from the sea
  (and from the arena: the inner wall). Crest tops slope in, so anyone who got up there (vine chains) slides into
  the bowl, not out.
- **Stair fix (an old bug):** the stair's walk collider had a 51-54 deg lip at the east bend (the Catmull-Rom's heights
  bunched up there, and the ribbon folded on the inside of the bend): a captain walking it stopped dead. The heights
  are now even along each flight by flat distance, and the walk surface is a 0.4 m grid over the stair's corridor at
  the height of the line's nearest point (`_line_y`).
- **Clearances:** `RedtideFort.REACH` 100 m (was 45 no-go / 60 deep-water check): WorldGenerator's deep-water check
  (the spot is unchanged: deep to 130 m), the ships' no-go circle (so the sea's features keep off too), the patrol
  zone REACH + 45 (was 115), the arrival banner REACH + 15 (was 75). Redtide has no village; the jetty is its dock.
- **Per frame:** nothing new (static meshes and colliders; the massif ~4k tris, one mesh of 3-4 surfaces).
- **Tests:** t/world/redtide_way_in (the fort on the light stage, sea level = the ground: off the jetty up the stair
  into the arena; from the cliffs' foot at 11 spots running and jumping at the rock nobody gets up; drops over the
  crest, an arm and the arena land on rock). r8test (Morrow) green.

## 2026-11-03: 1.30 land fixes, piece 4: enemy toughness and co-op scaling (playtest row 8; v1_30_plan "Decided")
- `Net.hp_scale` is 1 + 0.85 per extra captain (x3.55 at four; was +0.6, x2.8). New `Net.dmg_scale` (+10% a captain
  past the first, applied in `Player.take_hit` to any attacker outside group "players", AI captains included) and
  `Net.poise_scale` (+0.5 a captain). Static `*_scale_for(n)` forms for tests.
- `Poise.cap()`: a foe's `full` x Net.poise_scale, read as hits land (so it follows the roster with nothing per
  frame); `Poise.make("player")` (a captain's own) never scales. The beasts' own thresholds (JungleBeast._poise_max,
  the Brood Queen's POISE) scale the same.
- Stronghold bosses (StrongholdBoss): `hp_k = hp x Net.hp_scale()` at spawn, and `rescale(k)` on the host's 0.25 s
  check when the crew changes (keeps the share of health left). They had no co-op scaling at all.
- `PirateGrunt.CREW_HP_K` 1.3 (`_crew_k()`): pirate crews, captains and marines +30% health for everyone; the
  drowned override it to 1. Morrow (his own BOSS_HP) and the ape (its own _max_hp) are unchanged solo.
- Tests: t/combat/coop_scaling (the numbers, a fake four-captain roster for Poise.cap and dmg_scale), t/stronghold/vane
  (rescale keeps him full at x2.7). nettest modes are affected (enemy health and damage in co-op): the lead's prepush.
- **Piece 3, no Admiralty spawn hitch (Admiralty):** the blockade, the ring and patrols no longer build every ship and
  crew in one frame. `_queue` adds the spec and starts its crew's bodies on a worker (`Humanoid.prebuild` of
  `EnemyShip.crew_plan`); `_process` makes the first waiting ship (`_pending`, in order) once `prebuilt_for` all her
  men, at most one a frame, then `Net.spawned`. Ahead: a deed books the ring's seeds and starts its crews at once
  (`ring_due.plan`, `_plan_for` reuses booked seeds whose kind still matches at `_close_ring`); a patrol's are booked
  PATROL_AHEAD 20 s before it sails (`_patrol_plan`). `net_gen` carries a third list, the ships on their way (the ring
  plan, the patrol plan, the pending), so guests prebuild them too; guests' `net_set_gen` queues new ships the same way
  and drops pending ones the host no longer has. A blockade ship made after her line broke gives chase (`break_line`);
  `_line_tick` and `_tidy` leave pending names alone. `_spawn` still makes one at once (tests). Gotcha: under a loaded
  machine the worker takes ~5 s for a blockade and ring (~45 bodies) where the deed comes with no warning: the
  booms and banner come first, the ships a few seconds later. Per frame: one `_pending.is_empty()` check.
  Tests: new t/ship/admiralty_warm (a deed's blockade and ring, then a patrol: no "a body built on the main thread" mark,
  one ship a frame); t/ship/admiralty_ring, admiralty_hunt, marine_chaser wait for the ships.
